clusters.headline_hint: Iran prepares terms for reopening Strait of Hormuz amid conflict with US

claims.text: The Australian government decided to withdraw 24 expeditioners from its Macquarie Island research station due to psychosocial risks posed by an expected H5 avian influenza mortality event.
A common dolphin found near Goolwa in South Australia tested positive for H5 bird flu, marking the second native mammal species in Australia confirmed to have contracted the virus.
Oil prices rose following reports that US President Donald Trump rejected re-establishing the terms of a June memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Operation Economic Outcast sanctions targeting nearly 60 Iran-linked individuals, entities, and vessels to pressure Iran amid war with the US.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned that if the US blockade continues, Iran will target US economic interests 100 percent, with intensity and force.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei stated that Iran has the legitimate right to target the origin of any act of aggression, pointing specifically to US refueling aircraft departing from Bulgaria.
Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran to discuss regional security and conditions for dialogue.
Mohsen Rezaei stated that Iran exported 80 million barrels of oil during the ceasefire period.
Mohsen Rezaei announced that Iran is drawing up a list of conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz after mediators asked Tehran to set out its terms.
Under a June Memorandum of Understanding, Iran agreed to clear mines and permit free vessel passage in the Strait of Hormuz for 60 days while the US agreed to lift its blockade and ease sanctions.
US President Donald Trump declared in the Oval Office that US forces had cleared mines from the Strait of Hormuz and that the waterway was open.
US President Donald Trump told Al Jazeera that he has no time schedule for negotiations with Iran and is in no hurry to resume talks.

US defence and NATO officials stated that the US military faces a critical shortage of Patriot missile interceptors in Europe due to interceptor stocks being redeployed to the Middle East for the war with Iran.
The Wall Street Journal reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow to warn Russia not to attack NATO countries.

clusters.headline_hint: Trump signs executive order directing federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

claims.text: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing the Department of the Interior to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America.
The US Geological Survey updated the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in its Geographic Names Information System following President Trump's order.
US President Donald Trump posted an altered 1948 Life magazine presidential ranking graphic on social media, placing himself at the top under a newly added category named greatest.

US President Donald Trump previously issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America, leading to a legal dispute with Mexico and an ongoing lawsuit by the Associated Press.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated in a social media post that Canadians know things must be called by their name and that the lake is called Lake Ontario today and forever.
Democratic Representative Debbie Dingell of Michigan announced plans to introduce legislation in Congress to nullify President Trump's order renaming Lake Ontario.
Canadian US trade minister Dominic LeBlanc stated on X that the US had withdrawn demands regarding French language labelling requirements.
The US imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods following the collapse of trade negotiations between Washington and Ottawa.
The name Lake Ontario originates from the Huron Indigenous word oniatari:io, meaning lake of shining waters.
Lake Ontario lies along the international border separating the US state of New York from the Canadian province of Ontario.

clusters.headline_hint: Meta reaches $17 billion settlement over child and teen safety claims on Facebook and Instagram

claims.text: Abrham Meareg filed a lawsuit in Kenya in 2022 alleging that Facebook's algorithm promoted posts calling for the murder of his father during northern Ethiopia's civil war.
Meta settled a lawsuit brought by 29 US states accusing it of designing addictive products for young people, agreeing to pay $18 billion and alter platform features in the US.
Meta agreed to pay $16.68 billion to settle claims from 29 US states alleging it designed its apps to addict teenagers and improperly harvested children's data.
In 2025, Meta's family of apps segment generated $198.8 billion in revenue and $102.5 billion in operating profit.
Instagram's user reach in India reached 481 million people in 2025, while Facebook's reach stood at 403 million.
Meta agreed to pay up to $17 billion in penalties to settle a landmark federal child safety lawsuit brought by California, Colorado, Kentucky, and New Jersey.

As part of its proposed settlement, Meta agreed to implement a default two-hour daily time limit for users under 18, a default block on nighttime use, and a ban on displaying like and reaction counts.
A glacier collapse in Nepal and Tibet triggered flash floods that killed at least 270 people and left more than 1,500 missing, including at least 65 Americans.
Meta reached a settlement agreement covering 47 states and several territories for up to $17.1 billion in penalties, alongside a separate $1 billion settlement in Texas.
Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers approved Meta's multi-state settlement agreement in federal court in Oakland, California.
British minister Pat McFadden stated that the UK government does not want a situation where children in the US receive a higher level of protection than children in the UK.

clusters.headline_hint: Devastating Himalayan glacial collapse triggers flash flood with hundreds dead and over 290 Indian pilgrims missing

claims.text: Nepal declined search and rescue team deployment offers from foreign countries following flash floods along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems.
India, China, the US, UK, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh offered to send rescue personnel to assist Nepal after the floods.
Nepal Police reported that 469 people died and 1,545 people were rescued or injured in the flash floods as of Friday.
Nepal Police deployed 4,348 personnel for search and rescue operations across affected districts.
Missing foreign nationals in Nepal include 178 Indians, 65 Americans, 51 Malaysians, 53 Ukrainians, 33 Britons, 35 Australians, and 25 Canadians.
The United States pledged $500,000 and the World Health Organization sent emergency medical supplies to support Nepal.
Nepali army helicopter rescue teams worked to rescue around 100 people trapped inside a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project.
Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that 555 stranded tourists and 499 local residents were transported out of the disaster zone in Tibet as of Friday morning.
Chinese state media reported that at least 558 people were missing on the Tibet side of the border, including at least 260 foreign nationals.
The Red Cross launched an emergency appeal for $31 million to respond to the disaster affecting an estimated 93,000 people.
UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher ordered the release of $2 million in emergency funds for flood relief.
Rakesh Nayak, a 45-year-old software engineer from Karnataka living in Australia, went missing near the Nepal-China border after flash floods swept the area during an Isha Foundation tour.
Rakesh Nayak was last known to be inside an immigration office near the Nepal-China border at around 9:10 pm on August 26, twenty minutes before flash floods struck.
At least 13 people from Karnataka are stranded in Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region following the flash floods.
The US Geological Survey clarified that the flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border was caused by a glacial collapse.
The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of the valley registered a seismic magnitude of 5.2.
An ICIMOD analysis found that an ice-rock avalanche entered the Lende Khola tributary, causing downstream river levels to rise by 7 to 9 metres within 30 minutes.
India's Ministry of External Affairs stated that 290 Indians in Nepal remain unaccounted for, while about 200 stranded on the Chinese side after the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra sought assistance.
The flash flood occurred in Nepal's northern Rasuwa district without prior rainfall in the immediate area to warn residents.

clusters.headline_hint: NCLT approval of Subhash Chandra's 99.97% debt haircut sparks political row and lender challenges

claims.text: The National Company Law Tribunal approved a personal insolvency repayment plan allowing Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra to pay Rs 6.5 crore against creditor claims of over Rs 22,000 crore.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticized the ruling on X, referring to the NCLT as the 'Neta-Company Loot Tribunal'.
Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh described the 99.97% debt reduction approved by NCLT as a 'mundan' that makes a mockery of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
Subhash Chandra's office stated that he was only a personal guarantor for corporate loans and had not borrowed money personally from creditors.
HDFC Bank stated it is exploring an appeal against the NCLT order granting a 99.97% haircut on personal guarantee claims against Subhash Chandra.
Subhash Chandra's net worth was estimated by the resolution professional at Rs 31.8 crore, of which Rs 25 crore consisted of his mortgaged house.
Creditors representing 80.8% of voting rights approved Subhash Chandra's repayment plan, while dissenting creditors represented around 15%.
Dissenting lenders argued that assenting creditors such as Veena Investments were related entities controlling over 61% of voting rights and were ineligible under Section 109(4)(b) of the IBC.
Former businessman Vijay Mallya posted on X congratulating Subhash Chandra while contrasting the settlement with recoveries in his own legal debt case.
Congress general secretary Randeep Singh Surjewala demanded the Finance Minister disclose 12 years of NCLT data, estimating total bank losses from haircuts could exceed Rs 10 lakh crore.

NCLT Member (Judicial) Nilesh Sharma approved Subhash Chandra's resolution plan under Section 114 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code as the third member following a split verdict by a two-member bench.
Under the approved plan, creditors are expected to recover approximately 0.028% of their original admitted claims, or about three paise for every Rs 100 owed.
For LIC Housing Finance's admitted claim of Rs 1,322.39 crore, the approved repayment amount was Rs 38,09,294.
Insolvency proceedings against Subhash Chandra were initiated in 2022 by Indiabulls Housing Finance over a defaulted Rs 170 crore loan to Vivek Infracon.
Subhash Chandra served as an Independent Rajya Sabha MP backed by the Bharatiya Janata Party from 2016 to 2022.

clusters.headline_hint: PM Modi to visit Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit and bilateral talks with Putin

claims.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will undertake a four-day visit to Uzbekistan from August 29 to 30 and the Kyrgyz Republic from August 31 to September 1.
PM Modi will hold delegation-level talks in Tashkent with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to strengthen their bilateral strategic partnership.
Bilateral trade and investments between India and Uzbekistan are close to $1 billion.
More than 16,000 Indian students are studying in Uzbekistan, which is home to four Indian university campuses.
PM Modi's Tashkent itinerary includes visits to the Lal Bahadur Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the SCO Summit in Bishkek.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar visited Moscow ahead of the summit to co-chair the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission meeting and meet President Putin.
PM Modi will attend the opening ceremony of the sixth World Nomad Games during his visit to Kyrgyzstan.
Russian President Vladimir Putin assured EAM S. Jaishankar during his Moscow visit that Russia would continue supplying fertilisers to help Indian farmers.
PM Modi is scheduled to host Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in India for the BRICS summit on September 12-13.
The upcoming summit in Bishkek marks the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, which India joined as a full member in 2017.
